Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government data exchange systems. 25 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Libya has Law No. 6/2022 on Electronic Transactions (providing data protection provisions, e-commerce, digital signatures) and Law No. 5/2022 on Combating Cybercrime. These provide a legal basis for electronic transactions and digital government operations. The National Authority for Information Security and Safety (NISSA) oversees authentication. No specific cross-government data sharing act exists, but these laws provide a partial framework.

revision_notes: All three cited sources were verified and are genuinely about Libya's Law No. 5/2022 (Cybercrime) and Law No. 6/2022 (Electronic Transactions) as described, but these are general e-transactions/data-protection laws, not legislation establishing cross-government data-sharing authority — the comment itself notes 'no specific cross-government data sharing act exists,' which does not support a code of 3 (Yes). The General Information Authority's own National Interoperability Plan (2026) confirms these 2022 laws only create a supportive legislative 'environment' and that Libya's national data-governance guide, open-data policy and a personal data protection law remain in draft/under-development. Revised to 2 (Under development), since a dedicated enabling instrument for the data exchange system does not yet exist but is being actively developed by GIA.
